findings.currentClaim: For an antiunitary exchange sending A=NN to A-dagger, i(A-A-dagger) is exchange odd.
findings.refereeResult: False: antiunitarity also sends i to -i, so both A+A-dagger and i(A-A-dagger) are even for the plus exchange convention used in 1391.
findings.requiredAction: Mark the antiunitary parity conclusion of 1291 superseded by 1391. Retain only its endpoint-blind no-go and its identification of the sterile bilinear as a conditional candidate under an additional unitary/phase convention.
findings.verifierAssessment: The 1291 verifier labels the candidate odd without implementing conjugate-linearity; it certifies its input convention, not the claimed antiunitary transformation.

findings.currentClaim: No finite four-dimensional operator derives three selected generations.
findings.refereeResult: Rank-nullity proves zero Fredholm index only for finite square maps. Rectangular complexes have an index equal to their dimension imbalance, and finite symmetry-protected kernels are not excluded by this proof.
findings.requiredAction: Replace the headline theorem by: no finite square internal map has nonzero Fredholm index; no currently supplied finite operator derives three rather than inserting multiplicity or extra protected data.
findings.verifierAssessment: Testing representative ranks is illustrative. The proof is the scoped rank-nullity argument, not the fixture.

findings.currentClaim: Tensoring the O(3)-twisted CP1 kernel with SM15 produces three four-dimensional chiral generations and the conjugate bundle is only the CAR adjoint.
findings.refereeResult: The index-three bundle statement is exact, but the physical conclusion also needs a declared six-dimensional Weyl parent or equivalent spectral polarization, its gauge representation, self-adjoint domain, and higher-dimensional anomaly audit. A six-dimensional Dirac parent generally supplies both product chiralities.
findings.requiredAction: Keep 1397 as an exact bundle-level bridge. Downgrade 1394's physical escape to a conditional index fixture until the parent chirality, CAR polarization, and higher-dimensional anomalies are constructed.
findings.verifierAssessment: Kernel dimensions and four-dimensional anomaly sums do not verify the higher-dimensional quantization or anomaly problem.

findings.currentClaim: The finite-slab fixture contains an exact tanh kink and has KK gap pi/(2L).
findings.refereeResult: The tanh profile reaches plus/minus u only asymptotically, so on [-L,L] it is a controlled approximation unless boundary data equal its finite endpoint values. The stated KK gap depends on an undeclared self-adjoint boundary condition and interval convention.
findings.requiredAction: Call the wall exact on the infinite line and exponentially accurate in the finite fixture. Declare the outer boundary conditions before quoting a KK gap or global folded spectrum.
findings.verifierAssessment: The verifier checks an allowed endpoint-tail tolerance and assumes the KK formula; this is not an exact finite-domain boundary-value solution.

findings.currentClaim: S_v1 contains a fully healthy quadratic benchmark.
findings.refereeResult: The calculation establishes positivity for a chosen bulk bosonic tree-level quadratic fixture. It does not cover fermions, boundary BRST/self-adjoint domains, loops, gravity, or the full interacting action.
findings.requiredAction: Use 'healthy scoped bosonic tree-level benchmark' and reserve 'fully healthy' for a complete field/domain/quantum audit.
findings.verifierAssessment: The verifier recomputes matrices from declared coefficients; it does not test global completion or radiative stability.

findings.currentClaim: The result is a laboratory-ready protocol.
findings.refereeResult: It is an experiment-design protocol: no device-specific effect size, calibrated noise budget, fabrication tolerances, power analysis, or demonstrated protected-Z3 platform is supplied.
findings.requiredAction: Replace 'laboratory-ready' by 'simulation-ready experiment design' until platform parameters and a power/noise budget are sourced.
findings.verifierAssessment: The verifier checks roots of unity, loop-phase invariance, and checklist completeness, not laboratory feasibility.

findings.currentClaim: The traceless threshold is scheme invariant while the full third direction is removed by a stress-tensor scheme choice.
findings.refereeResult: The demonstrated invariance is within the one-parameter improvement family of the free localized scalar fixture. Xi is also a curved-space Wilson coupling whose change can represent a different matched theory, not merely a renormalization convention. The cancellation shown is for an integrated response statistic, not necessarily every frequency-resolved spectral matrix.
findings.requiredAction: Say 'independent of xi within the displayed improvement family' and restrict the zero of the third direction to the integrated statistic actually computed.
findings.verifierAssessment: The scripts evaluate the declared vertex formula; they do not derive the Hilbert operator, operator mixing, or a microscopic matching for xi.

findings.currentClaim: The displayed DAG is the dependency frontier.
findings.refereeResult: Several edges are programme-workflow choices, not logical necessities: an analogue A11 experiment can precede A6/A9, and alternative chiral constructions need not depend on the current A5 branch.
findings.requiredAction: Type edges as logical, model-conditional, or workflow/prioritization dependencies. Call the current graph a candidate-action workflow DAG.
findings.verifierAssessment: The verifier proves only graph well-formedness and that the authored edges are present. It cannot certify their scientific necessity.

findings.currentClaim: Exact dualization and exact strict-IR BF description.
findings.refereeResult: The normalization is exact conditional on the stated compact-field conventions. The physical BF description is asymptotic/topological after integrating out massive modes and needs global-sector and boundary assumptions. The source also contains malformed expressions 'left[' and '3,da'.
findings.requiredAction: Use 'conditionally exact normalization' and 'strict-IR topological EFT'; repair the two displayed formula typos in a future correction pass.
findings.verifierAssessment: The verifier checks the chosen normalization, gaps, and orbifold ledger; it does not derive compactification or global boundary data.

findings.currentClaim: A complete finite selector model is constructed.
findings.refereeResult: It is a complete finite selector tuple/decision rule. The action couples to epsilon(T), a topology label not yet represented by a local operator or dynamical field.
findings.requiredAction: Replace 'model' by 'tuple' unless and until epsilon(T) is a local observable in the path integral.
findings.verifierAssessment: The verifier establishes anomaly sums, covariance of the stipulated tuple, and a compatible CP matrix; it does not construct the portal.

findings.currentClaim: The benchmark has zero same-chirality mirrors and a wide decoupling region.
findings.refereeResult: Zero mirrors is conditional on the unconstructed selector/CAR interpretation, and 'wide' is not quantified by one point plus continuity.
findings.requiredAction: Label mirror count as an assumption and replace 'wide' by 'nonempty open neighbourhood' unless a measure or scan is supplied.
findings.verifierAssessment: The script asserts the authored mirror count and checks one parameter point; it does not construct the fermionic Hilbert space.

findings.currentClaim: The one-loop audit determines the portal status.
findings.refereeResult: The document gives a complete spurion/counterterm classification in its restricted neutral boundary basis, not a one-loop integral or coefficient calculation. It also leaves the self-adjoint boundary domain open.
findings.requiredAction: Call it a one-loop symmetry/counterterm classification and avoid implying a computed beta function or finite threshold.
findings.verifierAssessment: The verifier correctly checks CAR and unitary/antiunitary parities; its numerical delta-M fixture is not a loop calculation.

findings.currentClaim: The verifier checks spontaneous CP vacuum degeneracy.
findings.refereeResult: The phase-circle/equivariance theorem is sound under the declared sterile rephasing, but evaluating a CP-even potential at theta and -theta does not establish that either point is a stationary vacuum.
findings.requiredAction: Keep the no-canonical-phase conclusion; describe the script as a potential-symmetry check unless stationary points and Hessians are also solved.
findings.verifierAssessment: The candidate-principle ledger is an audited input, not independently discoverable by the script.

findings.currentClaim: The scalar reads holonomy through stress.
findings.refereeResult: The computed matrices are gradient/strain occupation covariances, not the complete Hilbert stress susceptibility; contact, improvement, and port normalization are absent and are only partly repaired by 1393.
findings.requiredAction: Cite 1228 as a finite-regulator gradient-stress toy and use 1393/1396 for the physical-stress qualification.
findings.verifierAssessment: The script genuinely recomputes the finite lattice sums and ranks, but only for the stipulated toy observable.

findings.currentClaim: CP-conjugate sectors are degenerate for same-parity probes, while a mixed-parity/oriented spectral reader can supply a third toy direction.
findings.refereeResult: Valid within the stated finite/free fixtures. It does not solve A5 or define a physical stress port, and both documents say so.
findings.requiredAction: No status change; preserve the scope clauses.
findings.verifierAssessment: These scripts recompute nontrivial spectra, covariance/spectral positivity, CP relations, and response rank.

findings.currentClaim: The classical stress ledger is conditional, and the selected-projector completion canonically carries an O(3) bundle of index three while the physical fermion bridge is absent.
findings.refereeResult: Both stopping boundaries are correctly stated. The 1232 verifier is primarily a ledger certificate; the 1397 bundle calculation is substantive but remains nonphysical without the vertical fermion operator.
findings.requiredAction: No status change; do not promote either result beyond its declared boundary.
findings.verifierAssessment: 1397 independently recomputes degrees and kernel dimensions; 1232 mostly checks authored classifications.
